name: SGP126512 (Hubble)
blurb: SGP126512, an isolated elliptical galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: sgp126512-hubble
story: A lone elliptical galaxy far from the crowded clusters where most ellipticals live. Hubble imaged it to learn whether life in a cosmic void leaves its mark on fine details such as shells, dust lanes and nuclear disks.

claims.text: SGP126512 is a target of HST program 10630 at RA 23 24 10.13, Dec -31 09 29.29, matching this pointing (RA 351.0422, Dec -31.1581); coordinates from the 2dFGRS
The program studies truly isolated elliptical galaxies in voids identified with the 2dFGRS
Knowledge of ellipticals is biased toward overdense regions such as clusters
The program looks for fine-structure features such as nuclear disks, dust lanes and shells, which may differ for void galaxies
